observation.visible_scene: A nighttime outdoor shot under a warm yellow streetlight positioned at the top-center/right of the frame. The light casts a hazy glow over dark green foliage that fills the background, with a cluster of brighter yellow-green leaves in the lower-left corner and a thin vertical lamppost pole running down the right edge. Heavy rain is falling, rendered as many short, bright vertical streaks against the dark backdrop.
visible_changes: Rain streaks continuously move downward across the whole frame from the first to the last sampled image, indicating ongoing rainfall rather than a start or stop.

At scattered moments a single large, bright, out-of-focus droplet (a vertical blurred smear) appears at different horizontal positions near the middle of the frame (e.g. mid-left, center, right) and travels downward, consistent with drops passing very close to the lens and catching the light.
The streetlight glow, the right-side pole, and the lower-left leaves remain in essentially fixed screen positions throughout, so the scene's static elements do not translate.
No editing cut is visible; the sequence reads as one continuous shot.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the rain is falling onto (ground, pavement, water) is not visible.
The cause of the rain and any change in intensity before or after this segment are unknown.
Whether the light source flickers or stays constant beyond this excerpt cannot be determined.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is minimal; background elements stay aligned, suggesting a static or near-static handheld framing, but a very slight drift cannot be fully ruled out.

Individual rain streaks cannot be tracked reliably between adjacent frames due to their density and motion blur, so per-drop trajectories are inferred from the overall downward pattern rather than matched one-to-one.
